# Overview

**The question.** The luciferase assays normalise a HiBiT or NanoLuc reporter
against firefly. That only works if firefly is *not itself* eIF3d-dependent -
dividing by a co-regulated control subtracts part of the effect being measured.
So: where does firefly sit in the distributions that the eIF3d models rank
highest, relative to the four synonymous NanoLuc constructs it is meant to
normalise?

**Three axes, chosen because they are what the models use.** GC3 (synonymous
codon choice), CDS length, and 5'UTR length. Each is drawn as the expressed
MDA-MB-231 transcriptome and the eIF3d hypoxia-promoted set, with a reference
line per construct.

**Terms used below.**

* *expressed set* - the feature matrix's one transcript per gene, restricted to
  transcripts with a complete CDS (in frame, terminal stop present; GENCODE
  `cds_end_NF` dropped).
* *promoted set* - genes with `te_lfc > 0.5` and `te_padj < 0.05` in the si3d
  hypoxia 1hr contrast. Positive `te_lfc` means eIF3d **promotes**, because
  these files carry the `sictrl_vs_si3d` coefficient despite the filename
  stating the ratio the other way round. Asserted below on EIF3D's own
  `rna_lfc`.
* *the four constructs* - the synonymous NanoLuc variants in
  `accessories/transcribed_plasmids.xlsx`: `parent_bidir`, its codon-shuffled
  `negative_control_3d`, `3d-adapted` (GC3 driven down) and `3d-anti_adapted`
  (GC3 driven up). All four share one 5'UTR, one 3'UTR, one protein and one CDS
  length; only the codons differ.

**Firefly's 5'UTR is `r params$ff_utr5_annotated` nt, from the vector
annotation.** The firefly transcript carries the same CMV backbone and the same
5'UTR intron as the four NanoLuc constructs. Transcription starts
`r params$ff_utr5_retained` nt upstream of the ATG (section 3 locates the TSS
from a CMV landmark rather than assuming it), and the Promega annotation of this
vector gives the intron as the 226 nt that section 3 locates, leaving a
**`r params$ff_utr5_annotated` nt** mature 5'UTR. That is the single value
plotted. The vector annotation is the primary evidence for its own construct, so
it is what this notebook uses.

**One recorded caveat, which does not change the plotted value.** The firefly
copy of the intron differs from the NanoLuc copy by a `CAGG` deletion at the 3'
splice site, so the annotated intron's last two nt are `CA`, not the `AG` a
canonical acceptor needs; the nearest downstream `AG` is 13 nt further on.
Section 3 reports this and the 5'UTR it would imply, and asserts nothing that
contradicts the annotation. It is noted because it is the kind of detail that
would otherwise be rediscovered later, and because resolving it definitively
needs RT-PCR, RNA-seq or a sequenced transcript rather than more sequence
reading. The difference is under 0.1 log2 units and under one percentile point
of the 5'UTR distribution, which section 6 reports, so no conclusion in this
notebook turns on it.

# 1. Libraries

```{r load_libraries}
library(tidyverse)

source(here("code", "cds_reporter_design", "reporter_helpers.R"))
```

```{r param_checks}
lfc_cutoff  <- 0.5
padj_cutoff <- 0.05

stopifnot(
  "firefly 5'UTR params must be positive lengths" =
    params$ff_utr5_annotated > 0 && params$ff_utr5_retained > 0,
  "the unspliced 5'UTR must be the longer of the two" =
    params$ff_utr5_retained > params$ff_utr5_annotated,
```

# 2. Construct sequences

The four NanoLuc constructs come from the derived table
`33a_parse_plasmid_sequences.R` writes, so this notebook inherits every check
that script makes (intron spliced and verified as a single GT..AG match, the
four confirmed as synonymous variants of one backbone, each CDS still carrying
its designed sequence from the codon-adaptation notebook). Firefly is parsed
from the same spreadsheet here, because that script deliberately does not emit
it.

```{r load_constructs}
PARSED <- here("accessories", "transcribed_plasmids_parsed.csv")
stopifnot(
  "transcribed_plasmids_parsed.csv is missing - run 33a_parse_plasmid_sequences.R first" =
    file.exists(PARSED))

nl4 <- read_csv(PARSED, show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(
  "the four NanoLuc constructs are not all present" =
    setequal(nl4$construct, c("parent_bidir", "negative_control_3d",
                              "3d-adapted", "3d-anti_adapted")),
  # These are the properties that make them a controlled synonymous comparison.
  # Re-asserted here so this notebook fails on its own if the table is rebuilt.
  "the four constructs no longer share one CDS length" =
    n_distinct(nl4$cds_nt) == 1,
  "the four constructs no longer share one 5'UTR length" =
    n_distinct(nl4$utr5_nt) == 1
)
cat(sprintf("Four NanoLuc constructs: CDS %d nt, spliced 5'UTR %d nt (shared)\n",
            nl4$cds_nt[1], nl4$utr5_nt[1]))
```

```{r load_firefly}
clean_seq <- function(x) toupper(gsub("[^A-Za-z]", "", x))

sheet <- read_excel(here("accessories", "transcribed_plasmids.xlsx")) %>%
  transmute(construct, tx = clean_seq(transcribed_seq), cds = clean_seq(CDS))

FF <- "firefly luc"
stopifnot(
  "the firefly row is missing from the spreadsheet" = FF %in% sheet$construct,
  "sequences contain non-ACGT characters" =
    all(strsplit(paste0(sheet$tx, sheet$cds, collapse = ""), "")[[1]] %in%
          c("A", "C", "G", "T"))
)

ff_tx  <- sheet$tx[sheet$construct == FF]
ff_cds <- sheet$cds[sheet$construct == FF]

ff_hits <- gregexpr(ff_cds, ff_tx, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
stopifnot(
  "the firefly CDS does not occur exactly once in its transcript" =
    length(ff_hits) == 1 && ff_hits[1] > 0)
ff_cds_start <- ff_hits[1]

cat(sprintf("firefly: transcript %d nt, CDS %d nt starting at %d\n",
            nchar(ff_tx), nchar(ff_cds), ff_cds_start))
```

**Biological spot-check on the firefly ORF.** It must be luc2P - luc2 carrying
the same mouse ODC PEST degron the NanoLuc and Renilla lab constructs carry -
and not the PEST-less luc2, which is a prefix of it and so passes every length
and frame check. Asserted on the translated protein at both ends.

```{r firefly_spot_checks}
PEST_AA <- "SHGFPPEVEEQAAGTLPMSCAQESGMDRHPAACASARINV"
LUC2_N  <- "MEDAKNIKKGPAPFYPLEDGTAGEQLHKAMKRYALVPGTIAFTDAHIE"

stopifnot(
  "firefly CDS length is not a multiple of 3" = nchar(ff_cds) %% 3 == 0,
  "firefly CDS does not start with ATG"       = substr(ff_cds, 1, 3) == "ATG",
  "firefly CDS does not end in a stop codon"  =
    substr(ff_cds, nchar(ff_cds) - 2, nchar(ff_cds)) %in% c("TAA", "TAG", "TGA")
)

ff_sense <- substr(ff_cds, 1, nchar(ff_cds) - 3)   # stop stripped
ff_aa    <- as.character(translate(DNAString(ff_sense)))

stopifnot(
  "firefly has an internal stop codon" = !str_detect(ff_aa, fixed("*")),
  "firefly does not encode the luc2 N-terminus"   = startsWith(ff_aa, LUC2_N),
  "firefly is missing the C-terminal ODC PEST degron (luc2, not luc2P?)" =
    endsWith(ff_aa, PEST_AA)
)
cat(sprintf("firefly ORF: %d nt sense, %d aa, luc2 N-terminus and ODC PEST degron both present\n",
            nchar(ff_sense), nchar(ff_aa)))
```

# 3. The firefly 5'UTR: TSS and intron

**The TSS is located from the CMV landmark, not assumed.** The firefly entry in
the spreadsheet begins inside the CMV promoter, upstream of where transcription
starts. The landmark `GTTTAGTGAACCGTCAGAT` spans the start: the `GTCAGAT` inside
it is exactly where the four NanoLuc transcripts begin, and those are entered
from their TSS. So the same motif fixes firefly's.

```{r firefly_tss}
LANDMARK  <- "GTTTAGTGAACCGTCAGAT"
TSS_MOTIF <- "GTCAGAT"

lm_hits <- gregexpr(LANDMARK, ff_tx, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
stopifnot(
  "the CMV landmark does not occur exactly once in the firefly entry" =
    length(lm_hits) == 1 && lm_hits[1] > 0)

ff_tss <- lm_hits[1] + (regexpr(TSS_MOTIF, LANDMARK, fixed = TRUE) - 1L)

# The four NanoLuc transcripts are entered FROM the TSS, so their 5'UTR must
# begin with this motif. That is what licenses using it to locate firefly's.
stopifnot(
  "the NanoLuc 5'UTRs do not begin at the TSS motif - the landmark no longer anchors the start" =
    all(startsWith(nl4$utr5, TSS_MOTIF)))

ff_utr5_unspliced <- substr(ff_tx, ff_tss, ff_cds_start - 1L)

cat(sprintf("firefly TSS at position %d; %d nt of the entry sit upstream of it\n",
            ff_tss, ff_tss - 1L))
cat(sprintf("firefly unspliced 5'UTR: %d nt, begins %s, ends ...%s\n",
            nchar(ff_utr5_unspliced), substr(ff_utr5_unspliced, 1, 12),
            substr(ff_utr5_unspliced, nchar(ff_utr5_unspliced) - 11,
                   nchar(ff_utr5_unspliced))))

stopifnot(
  "the unspliced firefly 5'UTR is not the expected retained-intron length" =
    nchar(ff_utr5_unspliced) == params$ff_utr5_retained,
  # The construct's Kozak. If the CDS start were misplaced this would not hold.
  "the firefly 5'UTR does not end on the gccacc Kozak" =
    endsWith(ff_utr5_unspliced, "GCCACC")
)
```

**The intron, and the missing acceptor.** The intron sequence is taken from the
NanoLuc backbone, whose copy is intact, and the firefly copy is then located by
aligning on the shared upstream flank. The two differ, which is the point: the
firefly copy is 3 nt shorter at its 3' end and ends in `CA` rather than `AG`.
Combined with the `G` missing from the start of the downstream exon, that is the
`CAGG` deletion.

```{r firefly_intron}
# The intact intron, as the NanoLuc backbone carries it. Recovered from the
# parsed table by difference rather than transcribed: the parsed 5'UTR is the
# spliced one, and the spreadsheet entry is unspliced, so the intron is what
# splicing removed. Deriving it this way means a change to either file is
# caught here instead of silently disagreeing with a pasted constant.
nl_parent_tx <- sheet$tx[sheet$construct == "parent_bidir"]
nl_parent_u5 <- nl4$utr5[nl4$construct == "parent_bidir"]

nl_u5_unspliced <- substr(nl_parent_tx, 1,
                          gregexpr(nl4$cds[nl4$construct == "parent_bidir"],
                                   nl_parent_tx, fixed = TRUE)[[1]][1] - 1L)

# The spliced 5'UTR is the unspliced one with one internal block removed, so the
# intron's LENGTH is known by difference. Its POSITION is not: a greedy shared
# prefix overshoots the donor here, because the intron and the downstream exon
# both begin GT. So every position whose removal reproduces the spliced 5'UTR is
# enumerated, and the GT..AG rule picks among them.
intron_n <- nchar(nl_u5_unspliced) - nchar(nl_parent_u5)
stopifnot("the spliced and unspliced NanoLuc 5'UTRs are the same length" =
            intron_n > 0)

excise <- function(s, p, n) paste0(substr(s, 1, p - 1L),
                                   substr(s, p + n, nchar(s)))
cand <- Filter(
  function(p) excise(nl_u5_unspliced, p, intron_n) == nl_parent_u5,
  seq_len(nchar(nl_u5_unspliced) - intron_n + 1L))
stopifnot("no excision of the expected length reproduces the spliced 5'UTR" =
            length(cand) > 0)

gt_ag <- Filter(function(p) {
  b <- substr(nl_u5_unspliced, p, p + intron_n - 1L)
  startsWith(b, "GT") && endsWith(b, "AG")
}, cand)
stopifnot(
  "no GT..AG intron of the expected length reproduces the spliced 5'UTR" =
    length(gt_ag) == 1)

pre_n     <- gt_ag[[1]] - 1L
NL_INTRON <- substr(nl_u5_unspliced, gt_ag[[1]], gt_ag[[1]] + intron_n - 1L)

cat(sprintf("%d excision position(s) of %d nt reproduce the spliced 5'UTR; %d obeys GT..AG\n",
            length(cand), intron_n, length(gt_ag)))
stopifnot(
  "the recovered NanoLuc intron does not reconstitute the unspliced 5'UTR" =
    excise(nl_u5_unspliced, pre_n + 1L, intron_n) == nl_parent_u5,
  "the recovered NanoLuc intron does not obey the GT..AG rule" =
    startsWith(NL_INTRON, "GT") && endsWith(NL_INTRON, "AG")
)
cat(sprintf("NanoLuc intron recovered by difference: %d nt, GT..%s\n",
            nchar(NL_INTRON), substr(NL_INTRON, nchar(NL_INTRON) - 1,
                                     nchar(NL_INTRON))))

# Locate firefly's copy on the shared upstream flank. The flank is taken from
# the NanoLuc intron's own context, so nothing is pasted in.
FLANK_N <- 12L
flank <- substr(nl_u5_unspliced, pre_n - FLANK_N + 1L, pre_n)

ff_flank_hits <- gregexpr(flank, ff_utr5_unspliced, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
stopifnot(
  "the shared pre-intron flank is not unique in the firefly 5'UTR" =
    length(ff_flank_hits) == 1 && ff_flank_hits[1] > 0)
ff_intron_start <- ff_flank_hits[1] + FLANK_N

cat(sprintf("shared pre-intron flank %s: NanoLuc at %d, firefly at %d (linker differs by %d nt)\n",
            flank, pre_n + 1L, ff_intron_start,
            ff_intron_start - (pre_n + 1L)))
```

```{r firefly_acceptor}
# How far the firefly copy tracks the NanoLuc intron before diverging.
ff_from_donor <- substr(ff_utr5_unspliced, ff_intron_start,
                        nchar(ff_utr5_unspliced))
shared_n <- 0L
while (shared_n < nchar(NL_INTRON) &&
       substr(ff_from_donor, shared_n + 1L, shared_n + 1L) ==
       substr(NL_INTRON, shared_n + 1L, shared_n + 1L)) shared_n <- shared_n + 1L

stopifnot(
  "the firefly intron copy does not begin with a GT donor" =
    startsWith(ff_from_donor, "GT"),
  "the firefly and NanoLuc introns diverge too early to be the same element" =
    shared_n > 150L
)
cat(sprintf("firefly tracks the NanoLuc intron for %d of its %d nt, then diverges\n",
            shared_n, nchar(NL_INTRON)))

cat(sprintf("the divergence is internal, not at the 3' end: firefly's copy runs %d nt in total\n",
            nchar(ff_from_donor)))
```

**The annotated intron is the Promega annotation for this vector**, held as an
explicit constant and then *located* in the transcript rather than trusted - the
same pattern `33a_parse_plasmid_sequences.R` uses for the NanoLuc intron. The
length cannot be derived from where the two copies diverge, because the
divergence is internal (an `AGC` to `AAG` change partway through) rather than at
the 3' end, so the annotation is the source for it. The mature 5'UTR is the
unspliced one minus this block.

```{r firefly_annotated_utr5}
# Promega's annotated 5'UTR intron for the firefly vector. Asserted below to
# occur exactly once in the unspliced 5'UTR, wholly inside it, with a GT donor.
FF_INTRON <- paste0(
  "GTGAGTACTCCCTCTCAAAAGCGGGCATGACTTCTGCGCTAAGATTGTCAGTTTCCAAAAACGAGGAGGATTTGATAT",
  "TCACCTGGCCCGCGGTGATGCCTTTGAGGGTGGCCGCGTCCATCTGGTCAGAAAAGACAATCTTTTTGTTGTCAAGTT",
  "GAGGTGTGGCAGGCTTGAGATCTGGCCATACACTTGAGTGACAATGACATCCACTTTGCCTTTCTCTCCA")

ff_int_hits <- gregexpr(FF_INTRON, ff_utr5_unspliced, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
stopifnot(
  "the annotated firefly intron does not occur exactly once in the unspliced 5'UTR" =
    length(ff_int_hits) == 1 && ff_int_hits[1] > 0)

# It must sit at the donor position the shared flank independently located.
stopifnot(
  "the annotated intron does not start at the donor the shared flank locates" =
    ff_int_hits[1] == ff_intron_start)

ff_intron_len   <- nchar(FF_INTRON)
ff_utr5_annot_n <- nchar(ff_utr5_unspliced) - ff_intron_len

cat(sprintf("annotated intron %d nt at position %d, last 2 nt = %s\n",
            ff_intron_len, ff_int_hits[1],
            substr(FF_INTRON, ff_intron_len - 1L, ff_intron_len)))

cat(sprintf("annotated intron %d nt -> mature firefly 5'UTR %d nt (unspliced %d nt)\n",
            ff_intron_len, ff_utr5_annot_n, nchar(ff_utr5_unspliced)))

stopifnot(
  "the firefly 5'UTR derived from the annotated intron is not the expected length" =
    ff_utr5_annot_n == params$ff_utr5_annotated,
  "the annotated intron must lie wholly inside the 5'UTR" =
    ff_intron_start + ff_intron_len - 1L <= nchar(ff_utr5_unspliced),
  "the annotated intron does not begin with a GT donor" =
    startsWith(FF_INTRON, "GT"),
  # It is the firefly copy, not the NanoLuc one: the two must differ, or the
  # wrong sequence has been pasted in.
  "the annotated firefly intron is identical to the NanoLuc intron" =
    FF_INTRON != NL_INTRON
)
```

**The caveat, recorded and not acted on.** The annotated intron's 3' end is `CA`
rather than `AG`, because the firefly copy carries a `CAGG` deletion relative to
the NanoLuc backbone. The nearest downstream `AG` is reported below together
with the 5'UTR it would imply. Nothing downstream uses it; it is here so the
observation is written down with its numbers rather than rediscovered.

```{r firefly_acceptor_caveat}
annot_end <- substr(ff_from_donor, ff_intron_len - 1L, ff_intron_len)
cat(sprintf("annotated intron ends in %s (a canonical acceptor would be AG)\n",
            annot_end))

ag_pos <- NA_integer_
for (i in seq(ff_intron_len - 1L, nchar(ff_from_donor) - 1L)) {
  if (substr(ff_from_donor, i, i + 1L) == "AG") { ag_pos <- i + 1L; break }
}

if (is.na(annot_end) || annot_end == "AG") {
  cat("  the annotated 3' end is already AG; no caveat applies\n")
} else {
  stopifnot("no downstream AG found in the firefly 5'UTR" = !is.na(ag_pos))
  cat(sprintf("  nearest downstream AG ends %d nt further on: intron %d nt -> 5'UTR %d nt\n",
              ag_pos - ff_intron_len, ag_pos,
              nchar(ff_utr5_unspliced) - ag_pos))
  cat(sprintf("  plotted value stays %d nt, from the vector annotation\n",
              params$ff_utr5_annotated))
}
```

# 4. Gene sets

Built exactly as in `01_`, `08_` and `13_`, repeated rather than inherited so
this notebook fails on its own if the contrast or the matrix changes.

```{r load_promotes}
te_hyp <- read_csv(
  here("output", "translation_categories_si3d_vs_sictrl_hypoxia_1hr.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE)

# Direction check. These files hold the sictrl_vs_si3d coefficient despite the
# filename stating the ratio the other way round, so positive te_lfc = eIF3d
# promotes. EIF3D's own rna_lfc must be strongly positive because the siRNA
# depletes its target.
eif3d_rna <- te_hyp %>% filter(symbol == "EIF3D") %>% pull(rna_lfc)
stopifnot("EIF3D rna_lfc is not strongly positive: contrast direction may be flipped" =
            length(eif3d_rna) == 1 && eif3d_rna > 2)
cat("Direction check - EIF3D rna_lfc:", round(eif3d_rna, 2), "\n")

promotes <- te_hyp %>%
  filter(te_lfc > lfc_cutoff, te_padj < padj_cutoff) %>%
  mutate(gene_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", gene_id))
stopifnot("Expected 1604 eIF3d hypoxia-promoted genes" = nrow(promotes) == 1604)
cat("eIF3d hypoxia 1hr promoted genes:", nrow(promotes), "\n")
```

```{r transcripts}
fm <- readRDS(here("output", "predictive_modeling",
                   "feature_matrix_external_stability.rds"))
tx_all      <- fm %>% dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, gene_id_clean, symbol)
tx_promotes <- tx_all %>% filter(gene_id_clean %in% promotes$gene_id_clean)

missing_gene_ids <- promotes$gene_id_clean[
  !promotes$gene_id_clean %in% tx_all$gene_id_clean]

tx_map <- read_tsv(
  here("accessories", "human", "tx2gene_hs_dm_v49_r111.tsv.gz"),
  col_names = c("transcript_id", "gene_id"), col_types = "cc") %>%
  filter(str_starts(transcript_id, "ENST")) %>%
  transmute(transcript_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", transcript_id),
            gene_id_clean       = sub("\\..*", "", gene_id))

hyp_samples <- c("NM2025_0094", "NM2025_0095", "NM2025_0096")
hyp_files   <- setNames(
  file.path(here("2025_MDAcells_riboseq", "salmon"), hyp_samples, "quant.sf.gz"),
  hyp_samples)
stopifnot("Hypoxia siCTRL quant files missing" = all(file.exists(hyp_files)))

extra_tx_df <- map_dfr(names(hyp_files), function(s) {
  read_tsv(hyp_files[[s]], col_types = "cdddd",
           col_names = c("Name", "Length", "EffectiveLength", "TPM", "NumReads"),
           skip = 1) %>% dplyr::select(Name, TPM)
}) %>%
  group_by(Name) %>% summarise(mean_tpm = mean(TPM), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(transcript_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", Name)) %>%
  inner_join(tx_map, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>%
  filter(gene_id_clean %in% missing_gene_ids, mean_tpm > 0) %>%
  group_by(gene_id_clean) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(mean_tpm, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(promotes %>% dplyr::select(gene_id_clean, symbol) %>% distinct(),
            by = "gene_id_clean") %>%
  dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, gene_id_clean, symbol)

tx_promotes <- bind_rows(tx_promotes, extra_tx_df)
cat(sprintf("Promoted transcripts: %s (%s recovered from salmon)\n",
            fmt_n(nrow(tx_promotes)), fmt_n(nrow(extra_tx_df))))
```

# 5. Gene metrics

```{r cds_metrics}
TXDB <- here("accessories", "human", "txdb.gencode49.sqlite")
cds_metrics <- build_cds_metrics(TXDB)

stopifnot(
  "Gene CDS GC% out of range"  =
    all(cds_metrics$gc_pct  >= 0 & cds_metrics$gc_pct  <= 100),
  "Gene CDS GC3% out of range" =
    all(cds_metrics$gc3_pct >= 0 & cds_metrics$gc3_pct <= 100),
  "Gene CDS lengths must be divisible by 3" =
    all(cds_metrics$cds_length %% 3 == 0),
  # Project convention: GC3 median must sit in 40-65%.
  "Transcriptome GC3 median outside the expected 40-65% range" =
    between(median(cds_metrics$gc3_pct), 40, 65)
)
cat(sprintf("Transcriptome GC3 median: %.1f%%\n", median(cds_metrics$gc3_pct)))
```

```{r utr5_lengths}
txdb   <- AnnotationDbi::loadDb(TXDB)
u5     <- fiveUTRsByTranscript(txdb, use.names = TRUE)
u5_len <- sum(BiocGenerics::width(u5))
names(u5_len) <- sub("\\..*", "", names(u5_len))

stopifnot(
  "Duplicate transcript IDs after version stripping" =
    !any(duplicated(names(u5_len))),
  "A 5'UTR length is not a positive integer" =
    all(u5_len > 0) && all(u5_len == as.integer(u5_len))
)
utr5_all <- tibble(transcript_id_clean = names(u5_len),
                   utr5_length = as.integer(u5_len))

# Verified against a column that already exists, rather than trusting either.
check <- fm %>%
  transmute(transcript_id_clean, fm_len = as.numeric(utr5_length)) %>%
  inner_join(utr5_all, by = "transcript_id_clean")
stopifnot(
  "The feature matrix and the TxDb disagree on 5'UTR length" =
    all(check$fm_len == check$utr5_length),
  "Too few transcripts matched to make the check meaningful" = nrow(check) > 5000
)
cat(sprintf("5'UTR extraction verified against the feature matrix: %s transcripts, max deviation %g\n",
            fmt_n(nrow(check)), max(abs(check$fm_len - check$utr5_length))))
```

```{r assemble}
# One table per group, carrying all three metrics, restricted to transcripts
# with a complete CDS so the three panels describe the same mRNAs.
metrics <- cds_metrics %>% inner_join(utr5_all, by = "transcript_id_clean")

expressed <- tx_all      %>% inner_join(metrics, by = "transcript_id_clean")
promoted  <- tx_promotes %>% inner_join(metrics, by = "transcript_id_clean")

cat(sprintf("Expressed: %s of %s transcripts carry a 5'UTR and a complete CDS\n",
            fmt_n(nrow(expressed)), fmt_n(nrow(tx_all))))
cat(sprintf("Promoted:  %s of %s\n",
            fmt_n(nrow(promoted)), fmt_n(nrow(tx_promotes))))

outside <- setdiff(promoted$transcript_id_clean, expressed$transcript_id_clean)
stopifnot(
  "A promoted transcript is outside the expressed set for a reason other than the salmon augmentation" =
    all(outside %in% extra_tx_df$transcript_id_clean),
  "Median 5'UTR length outside the expected 50-400 nt range" =
    between(median(expressed$utr5_length), 50, 400)
)
```

```{r spot_check_genes}
# Biological spot-check: the cytosolic ribosomal proteins have characteristically
# SHORT 5'UTRs and above-median GC3. If either extraction had picked up the wrong
# region or the wrong codon position, these orderings would not hold.
rp <- expressed %>% filter(str_detect(symbol, "^RP[SL]\\d"))
stopifnot(
  "Too few ribosomal protein genes for the spot-check" = nrow(rp) >= 50,
  "Ribosomal protein 5'UTRs are not shorter than the median: extraction suspect" =
    median(rp$utr5_length) < median(expressed$utr5_length)
)
cat(sprintf("Spot-check: %d ribosomal protein mRNAs, median 5'UTR %g nt vs %g nt transcriptome-wide\n",
            nrow(rp), median(rp$utr5_length), median(expressed$utr5_length)))
```

# 6. Reference lines

**The constructs are measured on the same bases as the genes.** CDS length and
total GC use the stop-stripped CDS; GC3 uses internal codons only (initiator and
stop removed), matching `gc3_internal` in the modelling, because GC3 exists to
measure synonymous choice and the forced initiator is not one. Those are the
`orf_gc_pct` / `orf_gc3_pct` helpers, so nothing here defines its own metric.

```{r reference_table}
ref <- bind_rows(
  nl4 %>% transmute(
    construct, cds_with_stop = cds, utr5_length = as.numeric(utr5_nt)),
  tibble(construct = "firefly",
         cds_with_stop = ff_cds, utr5_length = params$ff_utr5_annotated)
) %>%
  mutate(
    sense      = substr(cds_with_stop, 1, nchar(cds_with_stop) - 3),
    cds_length = nchar(sense),
    gc_pct     = map_dbl(sense, orf_gc_pct),
    gc3_pct    = map_dbl(sense, orf_gc3_pct)
  )

stopifnot(
  "Construct GC% out of range"  = all(ref$gc_pct  >= 0 & ref$gc_pct  <= 100),
  "Construct GC3% out of range" = all(ref$gc3_pct >= 0 & ref$gc3_pct <= 100),
  "Construct CDS lengths must be divisible by 3" = all(ref$cds_length %% 3 == 0),
  "Construct 5'UTR lengths must be positive"     = all(ref$utr5_length > 0)
)

# Biological spot-check: the designed GC3 ordering of the synonymous series.
g <- setNames(ref$gc3_pct, ref$construct)
stopifnot(
  "designed GC3 ordering is wrong: adapted < parent < anti-adapted expected" =
    g[["3d-adapted"]] < g[["parent_bidir"]] &&
    g[["parent_bidir"]] < g[["3d-anti_adapted"]],
  "the negative control should match the parent's GC3 (same codon composition)" =
    abs(g[["negative_control_3d"]] - g[["parent_bidir"]]) < 1e-9
)

print(as.data.frame(ref %>%
  dplyr::select(construct, cds_length, gc_pct, gc3_pct, utr5_length) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))))
```

```{r reference_style}
# Colors. Okabe-Ito orange (#E69F00) and sky blue (#56B4E9) are reserved
# project-wide for eIF3d and eIF3e and are not used to label a construct; orange
# is already the promoted-set curve here. Firefly keeps the bluish green it has
# in notebooks 62_ and 68_ so the panels are readable against those. The four
# NanoLuc constructs keep the hues 33_plasmid_predictions.Rmd gives them.
#
# parent_bidir and negative_control_3d are IDENTICAL on GC3 and CDS length by
# construction (the control is a synonymous shuffle of the parent), so a solid
# line would be completely hidden by the other. The control is dashed for that
# reason, not as decoration.
style <- tribble(
  ~construct,                   ~color,     ~linetype,
  "firefly",                    "#009E73",  "solid",
  "parent_bidir",               "black",    "solid",
  "negative_control_3d",        "black",    "dashed",
  "3d-adapted",                 "#D55E00",  "solid",
  "3d-anti_adapted",            "#0072B2",  "solid"
)
stopifnot("every construct needs a style" =
            setequal(style$construct, ref$construct))

ref <- ref %>%
  left_join(style, by = "construct") %>%
  mutate(construct = factor(construct, levels = style$construct)) %>%
  arrange(construct) %>%
  dplyr::rename(reporter = construct)

group_cols <- c("All expressed mRNAs"    = "grey70",
                "eIF3d hypoxia promotes" = "#E69F00")

fmt_nt  <- function(x) sprintf("%s nt", fmt_n(round(x)))
fmt_pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", x)
```

**What the plotted 5'UTR would have to be wrong by to matter.** The annotated
value is the one drawn; the alternatives from section 3's caveat are listed
beside it only to show the panel's reading does not turn on them.

```{r firefly_utr5_sensitivity}
pct_u5 <- function(v) c(
  expressed = 100 * mean(expressed$utr5_length <= v),
  promoted  = 100 * mean(promoted$utr5_length  <= v))

sens <- tibble(
  candidate = c("annotated intron (plotted)",
                "first downstream AG",
                "intron retained"),
  utr5_nt   = c(params$ff_utr5_annotated,
                nchar(ff_utr5_unspliced) - ag_pos,
                nchar(ff_utr5_unspliced))
) %>%
  mutate(log2_nt       = round(log2(utr5_nt), 2),
         pct_expressed = round(map_dbl(utr5_nt, ~ pct_u5(.x)[["expressed"]]), 1),
         pct_promoted  = round(map_dbl(utr5_nt, ~ pct_u5(.x)[["promoted"]]),  1))
print(as.data.frame(sens))

cat(sprintf("\nPlotted vs the acceptor alternative: %.2f log2 units and %.1f percentile points apart.\n",
            abs(sens$log2_nt[1] - sens$log2_nt[2]),
            abs(sens$pct_expressed[1] - sens$pct_expressed[2])))
```

The 5'UTR distribution is strongly right-skewed, so the same data on a log2
axis. **This is the readable one** - the linear panel spends most of its width
on a tail holding a few percent of the transcripts.

```{r panel_utr5_log2, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=5.5}
expressed_l <- expressed %>% mutate(log2_utr5_length = log2(utr5_length))
promoted_l  <- promoted  %>% mutate(log2_utr5_length = log2(utr5_length))
ref_l       <- ref       %>% mutate(log2_utr5_length = log2(utr5_length))

stopifnot("log2 transform changed the median 5'UTR length" =
            abs(2^median(expressed_l$log2_utr5_length) -
                  median(expressed$utr5_length)) < 1e-6)

p_u5_log <- plot_density_luc(
  expressed_l, promoted_l, "log2_utr5_length",
  xlab       = "log2 5'UTR length",
  title      = "log2 5'UTR length: firefly vs the four NanoLuc constructs, MDA-MB-231",
  outfile    = "cds_reporter_19_density_log2_utr5_length_firefly_vs_nanoluc.pdf",
  luc_tbl    = ref_l, group_cols = group_cols,
  metric_fmt = function(x) sprintf("%s nt", fmt_n(round(2^x))))
```

# 8. Percentiles

**A reference line is only interpretable with its percentile attached.** For
each construct and each metric: where it falls within the expressed
transcriptome, and within the eIF3d-promoted set.

```{r percentiles}
pct_of <- function(x, v) 100 * mean(x <= v)

pct_tbl <- ref %>%
  dplyr::select(reporter, cds_length, gc_pct, gc3_pct, utr5_length) %>%
  pivot_longer(-reporter, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    pct_expressed = pct_of(expressed[[metric]], value),
    pct_promoted  = pct_of(promoted[[metric]],  value),
    median_expressed = median(expressed[[metric]]),
    median_promoted  = median(promoted[[metric]])
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1)))

print(as.data.frame(pct_tbl))

OUTDIR <- here("output", "cds_reporter_design")
dir.create(OUTDIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write_csv(pct_tbl, file.path(OUTDIR, "19_firefly_vs_nanoluc_percentiles.csv"))
write_csv(ref %>% dplyr::select(reporter, cds_length, gc_pct, gc3_pct, utr5_length),
          file.path(OUTDIR, "19_firefly_vs_nanoluc_construct_properties.csv"))
cat("\nExported to output/cds_reporter_design/:\n",
    " 19_firefly_vs_nanoluc_percentiles.csv\n",
    " 19_firefly_vs_nanoluc_construct_properties.csv\n")
```

# 9. Where firefly sits

```{r summary}
ff_row <- pct_tbl %>% filter(reporter == "firefly")
nl_row <- pct_tbl %>% filter(reporter == "parent_bidir")

for (m in c("gc3_pct", "cds_length", "utr5_length")) {
  f <- ff_row %>% filter(metric == m)
  n <- nl_row %>% filter(metric == m)
  cat(sprintf("%-12s firefly %8.1f -> %4.1fth pct expressed, %4.1fth of promoted | parent NanoLuc %8.1f -> %4.1fth, %4.1fth\n",
              m, f$value, f$pct_expressed, f$pct_promoted,
              n$value, n$pct_expressed, n$pct_promoted))
}

# Wilcoxon, promoted vs every OTHER expressed transcript, for each metric. The
# disjoint comparison, matching what the panels report.
rest <- expressed %>% filter(!gene_id_clean %in% promoted$gene_id_clean)
cat("\nPromoted vs other expressed (Wilcoxon):\n")
for (m in c("gc3_pct", "cds_length", "utr5_length")) {
  wt <- wilcox.test(promoted[[m]], rest[[m]])
  cat(sprintf("  %-12s promoted median %8.1f vs %8.1f: p = %s\n",
              m, median(promoted[[m]]), median(rest[[m]]),
              format.pval(wt$p.value, digits = 3)))
}
```

**How to read this.** The eIF3d-promoted set is shifted relative to the rest of
the transcriptome on each of these axes (section 9 gives the direction and the
p-value). A reporter that sits deep inside the promoted set's range on the axes
that separate it is a reporter whose own translation may respond to eIF3d
depletion, which makes it a poor denominator. The percentile columns are the
quantity to compare, not the raw value: the three metrics have different units
and very different spreads.

**What this cannot tell you.** These are compositional features, not a
measurement. Firefly landing inside the promoted range means it *resembles* the
regulated mRNAs on features the models weight, not that it is regulated. The
direct test is firefly's own signal under si3d in the transfected cells, which
no sequence analysis substitutes for.
